key_idea: A conformal map onto a lens whose boundary pulls back to a uniform imaginary coordinate turns the volume product of a polytope into a sum of probabilities of feasible bases. A holomorphic mass estimate at an isolated zero bounds that sum below by 1, and a real feasible-simplex identity links it back to geometry.
reason: The complex-analytic route is striking and goes well beyond the standard toolkit: it encodes the volume product as an integral of feasible-simplex volumes and then bounds it by a holomorphic mass inequality. That reframing is a striking key idea with real explanatory content. However, the argument needs a lot of auxiliary machinery: lens asymptotics, measure-zero genericity lemmas, polytope approximation, a long equality analysis through lifted bodies, endpoint scaling and metric medians, and finally an appeal to the Hansen–Lima classification. That machinery buries the core and splits the proof into many moving parts.
